links.outcome: Readability grade level of ChatGPT responses to patient questions on hallux rigidus fusion
links.effect: Readability grade levels of 10.81 (ChatGPT-4o) vs. 10.37 (ChatGPT-5); responses above tenth-grade level.
links.quote: ChatGPT-4o generated longer responses (802 vs. 242 words; p<0.001) with slightly higher readability grade levels (10.81 vs. 10.37; p=0.031).

links.outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of AI-generated patient education responses
links.effect: Responses written at above tenth-grade reading level for patient information on hallux rigidus fusion surgery.
links.quote: ChatGPT-4o and ChatGPT-5 provide generally satisfactory yet non-comprehensive, limited-quality information at a level above tenth-grade regarding hallux rigidus fusion surgery.

links.outcome: Presence of citations, authorship, or transparency indicators in responses (JAMA benchmark score)
links.effect: All responses received a JAMA score of 0 due to absence of citations, authorship, or transparency indicators.
links.quote: All responses received a JAMA score of 0 due to the absence of citations, authorship, or transparency indicators.

screen.reason: Evaluates the readability and quality of responses from LLMs (ChatGPT-4o and ChatGPT-5) to patient questions regarding orthopedic surgery, without testing an organizational deployment safeguard or practice.
